title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering switching from Jira to Plane, likely due to Plane's self-hosted and free nature, which can be a key reason for teams looking to reduce costs or have more control over their data. The core use case for both tools is issue tracking and project management.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a proprietary tool with a per-user cost, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows for full data ownership since it's self-hosted, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Plane has a more complex setup process due to its self-hosted nature, while Jira offers a simpler, cloud-based setup.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while Plane's scalability depends on the server infrastructure.
* Integration: Jira has a more extensive list of integrations with third-party tools, while Plane has a more limited set of integrations, including GitHub and GitLab.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Jira:**
* Extensive list of integrations with third-party tools
* Scalable and reliable infrastructure
* User-friendly interface
* Robust project management features
* Good customer support
**Plane:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Full data ownership
* Customizable and flexible
* Open-source community
* Limited costs (only server costs)

## When to Choose Each
Jira is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require a scalable and reliable project management tool with a wide range of integrations. It's also a good choice for teams that don't mind paying a per-user cost and value the convenience of a cloud-based setup. Plane, on the other hand, is ideal for small to medium-sized teams or organizations that want full control over their data and are comfortable with a self-hosted solution. It's also a good choice for teams on a tight budget or those that value the flexibility and customizability of an open-source tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up your Plane server and configure the necessary settings.
3. Use the Plane import tool to migrate your data from Jira.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or customizations in Plane.
5. Test your setup and ensure that all data has been migrated correctly.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the features and polish of Jira. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Plane's integration with certain third-party tools is still limited. However, for teams that value self-hosting and full data ownership, Plane is a compelling alternative to Jira, and we recommend switching if you're a small to medium-sized team with simple project management needs and don't require a wide range of integrations.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need extensive integrations
* Teams that require full data ownership and self-hosting
* Organizations on a tight budget that can't afford Jira's per-user cost
* Teams that value the flexibility and customizability of an open-source tool
* Teams with simple project management needs that don't require a wide range of features

## FAQ
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, with no per-user costs.
### Can I migrate my Jira data to Plane?
Yes, you can export your Jira data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using the Plane import tool.
### Is Plane suitable for large teams?
No, Plane is not yet suitable for large teams, as it lacks some of the features and scalability of Jira.
### Can I integrate Plane with GitHub?
Yes, Plane has integration with GitHub and GitLab.
### Is Plane open-source?
Yes, Plane is open-source and released under the Apache 2.0 license.
meta_description: Plane, a free self-hosted project management tool, offers an alternative to Jira. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan

## Overview

Trello is a visual kanban board tool from Atlassian, simple and beginner-friendly. WeKan is an open-source kanban board offering the same card/list/board model without vendor dependency.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Trello paid plans start at $5/user/month; WeKan is completely free
- **Data control**: WeKan runs on your own server; Trello data lives on Atlassian infrastructure
- **Features**: Trello has a larger Power-Ups marketplace; WeKan covers core kanban features
- **Setup**: Trello requires zero setup; WeKan requires a server
- **Customization**: WeKan open-source code can be extended; Trello cannot

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Trello

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### WeKan

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [wekan/wekan](https://github.com/wekan/wekan) * ~20k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Trello if:** Trello suits individuals and small teams wanting instant zero-setup kanban with integrations to Slack, Google Drive, and GitHub.

**Choose WeKan if:** WeKan is ideal for teams wanting full data ownership or air-gapped deployments.

## Migration Path

Export Trello boards as JSON, then use WeKan Trello importer in Settings to recreate boards, lists, and cards.

## Our Take

WeKan is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Trello tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your WeKan instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Trello, switching to self-hosted WeKan will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Trello until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Trello paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is WeKan free to use?
Yes. WeKan is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Trello to WeKan?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Trello data, follow the WeKan import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does WeKan get regular updates?
Yes. WeKan has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use WeKan without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if WeKan development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Trello](https://trello.com) and [WeKan](https://wekan.github.io) before making decisions.*
meta_description: WeKan is a free, self-hosted alternative to Trello. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Dropbox and Nextcloud are cloud storage solutions that enable users to store, share, and collaborate on files. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and teams seeking to switch from a proprietary cloud storage service to a self-hosted or open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is file storage and sharing, and users may consider switching due to concerns over data ownership and cost.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Dropbox offers a range of pricing plans, while Nextcloud is free to use and self-host.
* Data ownership: Nextcloud allows users to maintain full control over their data, whereas Dropbox stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Dropbox is generally easier to set up, while Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Nextcloud can be more scalable than Dropbox, as users can add more storage and servers as needed.
* Integration: Nextcloud offers more extensive integration with other open-source tools, such as OnlyOffice for document editing, whereas Dropbox has tighter integration with Microsoft Office.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $9.99-$16.58/user/month (approx. $499.50-$829/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $9.99-$16.58/user/month (approx. $1,998-$3,316/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Dropbox:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Wide range of integrations with third-party apps
* Robust security features
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data storage and ownership
**Nextcloud:**
* Self-hosted and open-source
* High level of customizability and scalability
* Tight integration with other open-source tools
* Full control over data storage and ownership
* Can be complex to set up and maintain

## When to Choose Each
Dropbox is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams that require a user-friendly and straightforward cloud storage solution. It is ideal for teams that do not have the technical expertise or resources to self-host a cloud storage solution. On the other hand, Nextcloud is suitable for larger teams or organizations that require a high level of customizability, scalability, and control over their data. It is also a good choice for teams that value open-source software and self-hosting.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Dropbox using the Dropbox API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a Nextcloud server, either on your own hardware or using a cloud provider.
3. Use the Nextcloud import tool to migrate your data from the exported Dropbox files.
4. Configure your Nextcloud instance to meet your team's specific needs.
5. Test your Nextcloud setup to ensure that all features and integrations are working as expected.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready alternative to Dropbox for many users, offering a high level of customizability and control over data storage and ownership. However, it is essential to note that Nextcloud can be complex to set up and maintain, particularly for users without extensive technical expertise. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Nextcloud's scalability can be affected by the underlying server hardware and configuration. We recommend that teams with simple cloud storage needs and limited technical expertise stick with Dropbox, while larger teams or organizations with more complex requirements consider switching to Nextcloud.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with high data security requirements and limited budget
* Medium-sized teams with existing self-hosted infrastructure
* Large teams with complex cloud storage needs and extensive technical expertise
* Organizations with strict data ownership and control requirements
* Teams that require tight integration with other open-source tools

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud with my existing Dropbox account?
No, you will need to create a new Nextcloud account and migrate your data from Dropbox.
### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes, Nextcloud is free to use and self-host, but you will need to cover the cost of server hardware and maintenance.
### Can I integrate Nextcloud with Microsoft Office?
Yes, Nextcloud offers integration with Microsoft Office through the OnlyOffice plugin.
### Is Nextcloud more secure than Dropbox?
Nextcloud offers a high level of security and control over data storage and ownership, but the actual security of your setup depends on your server configuration and maintenance.
### Can I use Nextcloud on mobile devices?
Yes, Nextcloud offers mobile apps for Android and iOS devices.
meta_description: Nextcloud, a free self-hosted cloud storage solution, offers high customizability and control. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

- **Features**: Zoom has more enterprise features like webinars and AI tools; Jitsi covers core needs
- **Self-hosting**: Jitsi deploys on a small VPS in minutes; Zoom cannot be self-hosted

### How hard is it to migrate from Zoom to Jitsi Meet?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Zoom data, follow the Jitsi Meet import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Jitsi Meet get regular updates?
Yes. Jitsi Meet has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

# Microsoft Teams vs Mattermost (2026)

## Overview
Microsoft Teams and Mattermost are two popular team collaboration platforms that offer a range of features to enhance communication and productivity. This comparison is beneficial for teams and organizations looking to switch from Microsoft Teams to Mattermost, particularly those who value data ownership and self-hosting capabilities. The core use case for both tools is team collaboration, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Microsoft Teams offers a free plan, as well as paid plans starting at $6 per user per month, while Mattermost is free and open-source, with optional paid support.
* Data ownership: Mattermost allows teams to self-host their data, giving them full control and ownership, while Microsoft Teams stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Microsoft Teams is generally easier to set up, with a more streamlined onboarding process, while Mattermost requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Both platforms are highly scalable, but Mattermost's self-hosted option gives teams more control over their infrastructure.
* Integration with GitHub: Mattermost has native integration with GitHub, allowing for seamless collaboration and automation, while Microsoft Teams requires a third-party connector.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Microsoft Teams | Mattermost |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $6-$22/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT / AGPL |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $300-$1,100/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,200-$4,400/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Microsoft Teams:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Integrates well with other Microsoft tools
* Offers a range of features, including video conferencing and file sharing
* Has a large user community and plenty of support resources
* Can be expensive for large teams
**Mattermost:**
* Self-hosted option gives teams full control over their data
* Highly customizable and extensible
* Offers a range of features, including video conferencing and file sharing
* Has a strong focus on security and compliance
* Can be more difficult to set up and use, particularly for non-technical teams

# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Google Workspace and Nextcloud are two popular productivity and collaboration platforms that cater to different needs and use cases. Both tools offer a range of features, including email, calendar, and file sharing, but they differ significantly in terms of cost, data ownership, and setup complexity. The core use case for both tools is to provide a centralized platform for teams to collaborate and manage their work, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Google Workspace offers a range of pricing plans, starting at $6 per user per month, while Nextcloud is free and open-source, with optional paid support.
* Data ownership: Google Workspace stores data on its servers, while Nextcloud allows users to host their own data on their own servers.
* Setup complexity: Google Workspace is generally easier to set up and requires less technical expertise, while Nextcloud requires more technical knowledge to install and configure.
* Scalability: Google Workspace is designed to scale to meet the needs of large enterprises, while Nextcloud can also scale, but may require more effort and expertise to do so.
* Integration with third-party apps: Google Workspace has a wide range of integrations with third-party apps, while Nextcloud has a more limited range of integrations, but is highly customizable.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $300-$900/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,200-$3,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Google Workspace:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Wide range of integrations with third-party apps
* Scalable and reliable
* Good customer support
* Limited control over data and customization options
**Nextcloud:**
* Free and open-source
* Highly customizable and flexible
* Allows users to host their own data on their own servers
* Good for small to medium-sized teams and individuals
* Can be complex to set up and configure, limited support for large enterprises

## When to Choose Each
Google Workspace is a good choice for large enterprises and teams that require a scalable and reliable platform with a wide range of integrations with third-party apps. It is also a good choice for teams that are already familiar with Google's suite of productivity apps and want a seamless integration experience. Nextcloud, on the other hand, is a good choice for small to medium-sized teams and individuals who want a high degree of control over their data and customization options. It is also a good choice for teams that are looking for a free and open-source solution and are willing to invest time and effort into setting it up and configuring it.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Google Workspace using the Google Takeout tool, which allows you to download your data in a range of formats, including CSV and JSON.
2. Set up a Nextcloud server, either on your own hardware or using a cloud provider.
3. Use the Nextcloud import tool to import your data from Google Workspace, which supports a range of formats, including CSV and JSON.
4. Configure your Nextcloud instance to meet your specific needs, including setting up users and groups, and customizing the interface and features.
5. Test your Nextcloud instance to ensure that everything is working as expected and make any necessary adjustments.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready platform for most users, offering a high degree of control over data and customization options. However, it may not be the best choice for large enterprises that require a scalable and reliable platform with a wide range of integrations with third-party apps. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Nextcloud can be complex to set up and configure, especially for users without technical expertise. We recommend switching to Nextcloud if you are a small to medium-sized team or individual who wants a high degree of control over your data and customization options, and are willing to invest time and effort into setting it up and configuring it.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who want a free and open-source solution and are willing to invest time and effort into setting it up and configuring it.
* Individuals who want a high degree of control over their data and customization options.
* Teams that do not require a wide range of integrations with third-party apps.
* Teams that are looking for a self-hosted solution and are willing to invest in hardware and maintenance.
* Developers who want a highly customizable and flexible platform.

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud with my existing Google account?
No, Nextcloud requires you to create a new account and set up your own server. However, you can use the Google Drive app in Nextcloud to access your Google Drive files.
### Is Nextcloud compatible with all file types?
Nextcloud supports a wide range of file types, including documents, images, and videos. However, it may not support all file types, especially proprietary formats.
### Can I use Nextcloud on my mobile device?
Yes, Nextcloud has mobile apps for Android and iOS, allowing you to access your files and collaborate with your team on the go.
### Is Nextcloud secure?
Yes, Nextcloud takes security seriously and offers a range of features to protect your data, including encryption and two-factor authentication.
### Can I integrate Nextcloud with other apps?
Yes, Nextcloud has a range of integrations with third-party apps, including calendar and contact apps. However, the range of integrations is limited compared to Google Workspace.

# Airtable vs NocoDB

## Overview

Flexible spreadsheet-database hybrid for organizing anything. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. NocoDB is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Airtable costs Free / $10-$20/user/month; NocoDB is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Airtable is Proprietary; NocoDB is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: NocoDB can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: NocoDB eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: NocoDB has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Airtable | NocoDB |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $10-$20/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Airtable

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### NocoDB

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nocodb/nocodb](https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb) * ~45k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Airtable if:** Airtable is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose NocoDB if:** NocoDB is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Airtable in its standard export format, review NocoDB import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

NocoDB is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Airtable tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your NocoDB instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Airtable, switching to self-hosted NocoDB will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Airtable until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Airtable paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is NocoDB free to use?
Yes. NocoDB is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Airtable to NocoDB?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Airtable data, follow the NocoDB import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does NocoDB get regular updates?
Yes. NocoDB has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use NocoDB without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if NocoDB development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Airtable](https://airtable.com) and [NocoDB](https://nocodb.com) before making decisions.*
